reason: The FAQ sentence under 'Who should use AWS Control Tower?' states both routes (guided full enablement, or directly enabling AWS managed controls in an existing Organization); the claim paraphrases it exactly.
The quote states the native default directory, the post-setup option of a supported directory such as AWS Managed Microsoft AD, and self-managed access control.
The quote states recommended OUs, AWS Config and CloudTrail configuration, and guardrails enforcing policies across accounts.
The claim restates the quoted sentence word for word in substance.
The quote says to think of Organizations as the framework and Control Tower as the automation and governance layer; context says Control Tower builds upon Organizations.
The quote under the cost question states you also pay for underlying services that deploy controls, such as AWS Config rules for detective controls.
The quote says you can customize the Region deny control to apply regional restrictions that fit your business needs.
The claim restates the quoted sentence with the same scope.
The quoted note names guardrail as the previous term and control as the new term and says the terms are synonymous.
The three quotes state each category's purpose, and both strongly recommended and elective quotes say they apply at the OU level for all accounts in that OU.
The quote states the definition and the enterprise-wide container holding OUs, accounts, users and resources subject to compliance regulation.

No quote states the detective half of 'applies all mandatory preventive and detective controls' (only the preventive line is quoted), and the version condition (pre-4.0 vs 4.0) is not stated on this page; the quotes support the OUs, the Identity Center directory or self-managed IdP, and mandatory preventive controls.
Both quotes, under their account headings, state the log repository role and the restricted audit account with read and write access for security and compliance teams.
The quote supports only that all actions are logged including management and member accounts; 'automatically through CloudTrail and AWS Config' is in the preceding, unquoted sentence.
The claim restates the quoted bold sentence exactly.

The control's own text says it prevents CloudTrail configuration changes, and the LZ 4.0 change quote, with its list in context naming this control, says it is no longer deployed because it protected trails of LZ 2.9 and below.

The quotes state 'always applied' and 'can't be deactivated' without any version scope; the qualifier limiting this to landing zones before 4.0 comes from another fact and is not supported by these quotes, so the claim as scoped says more than the evidence.
The quotes support bucket policy, encryption and deletion protection for the log archive buckets; no quote covers the claimed logging and lifecycle configuration controls.
Both quoted sentences of the Note state the claim; the claim limits the manual removal to SCP and Config-rule controls, consistent with the hook-based exception in context.

The quotes support default VPC removal plus new VPC for new accounts and no new VPC for enrolled accounts; 'nor removes existing VPCs' and the Account Factory no-VPC condition appear only in unquoted context lines.
The quote states no additional charge and payment only for enabled and used services, with Service Catalog and CloudTrail as examples.
The quoted note states both parts of the claim.

The quote supports 'one operation at a time' with two exceptions, but does not name them; the optional-control and Account Factory exceptions are only in unquoted context lines, and 'per landing zone' scope is not stated.
The claim restates both quoted sentences.
The quotes support the organization-level trail and the per-account member trail before landing zone 3.0, but the date 2022-07-29 for version 3.0 is in no quote.
The quote states existing OUs with over 1000 directly nested accounts cannot be registered or re-registered; scope and condition match.
The preventive and detective control pages each state their half of the claim for an OU registered with Control Tower.
The three quotes define preventive, detective (with CloudTrail logging) and proactive controls (checked before provisioning, noncompliant not provisioned).

One quote says preventive controls are not applied to the management account; the other states the root user and admins can do work controls would deny and actions stay logged in the log archive account.
The quote states disallowing violating actions, the enforced or not enabled status, and support in all AWS Regions.
Both quotes state CloudFormation stack operations as the trigger and that direct console, API, SDK or other IaC requests may not be affected; the claim keeps 'may not'.
The quotes state scanning before provisioning, noncompliant resources not provisioned, and the PASS, FAIL or SKIP status.

The quotes support the Sandbox, Infrastructure (shared services and networking) and Workloads (production) OUs, but the Sandbox OU's purpose 'for development' is stated only in an unquoted context sentence.
The claim restates the three quoted sentences with the same scope.
The quote supports 'elective control with preventive guidance' and 'top-level control', but the added conclusion 'so it is not on unless you turn it on' is not stated by the quote.
The quoted Exceptions text states both the home Region rule and the IAM and Organizations exemption.
The quoted note states the loss of access to existing resources and the inability to deploy in denied Regions while enabled.
Both quoted bullets, under the landing zone Region deny considerations, state the two parts of the claim.
The quotes state enrolling existing accounts into a governed OU so controls apply, and registering existing OUs.
The quote states setting up and governing a multi-account environment with prescriptive best practices, orchestrating Organizations, Service Catalog and IAM Identity Center to build a landing zone.
